answer: Cipher computation proofs require every registered agent to solve a distinct, memory-hard cryptographic puzzle whose solution lifetime expires within minutes. An attacker scaling up a vine of thousands of clones faces linear hardware scaling costs because each parallel thread must independently solve the puzzle from scratch without caching. This makes mass replication economically unviable, as the continuous energy and compute expenditure of maintaining fake identities vastly exceeds the revenue a raven could harvest by honest participation.
